resources.string: Lets IntentLock notice when you open a guarded app (TikTok, Instagram, X) so it can show the pause screen. It only reads which app is in the foreground. It never reads your messages or screen content.
Breathe. If you leave, the timer starts over.
A forced pause before the apps that eat your time. Open one and a countdown blocks it; leave early and the countdown resets. The point is friction, not punishment.
Protection is NOT fully set up
Draw-over-apps: needed to show the pause screen
App detection: turn on IntentLock in Accessibility
Find \"IntentLock app guard\" and switch it on.
Delete protection: off (optional, adds friction to uninstall)
IntentLock asks to be a device admin so it can\'t be uninstalled on impulse. You can always remove it from this screen after the cooldown.
Turning this off removes the friction that stops impulsive deletes. Sure?
Protection is off — tap to re-enable
This does not delete the app — it lifts the pauses. To make sure it\'s a real decision and not an urge, there is a 24-hour wait. Tap again after 24 hours to finish.
